content: 1. Laxminarayan R, Matsoso P, Pant S, Brower C, Røttingen JA, Klugman K, et al. highlighted the global challenge of ensuring access to effective antimicrobials in their publication in The Lancet in 2016 (Volume 387, Issue 10014, Pages 167-175). 2. Pittet D, Sax H, Hugonnet S, and Harbarth S discussed the cost implications of successful hand hygiene promotion in their study published in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2004 (Volume 25, Issue 3, Pages 264-266). 3. Storr J, Twyman A, Zingg W, Damani N, Kilpatrick C, Reilly J, et al. presented the core components necessary for effective infection prevention and control programs, based on new WHO evidence-based recommendations, in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2017 (Volume 6, Article 6). 4. Kilpatrick CSJ, Zayed B, and Allegranzi B proposed a preliminary conceptual model exploring the relationship between two implementation approaches for preventing surgical site infections. This was published in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2017 (Supplement 3, Article O48). 5. Carayon P, Xie A, and Kianfar S examined the role of human factors and ergonomics as a patient safety practice in their article published in BMJ Quality & Safety in 2014 (Volume 23, Pages 196-205). 6. Wick EC, Hobson DB, Bennett JL, Demski R, Maragakis L, Gearhart SL, et al. described the implementation of a surgical comprehensive unit-based safety program aimed at reducing surgical site infections in their study published in Journal of the American College of Surgeons in 2012 (Volume 215, Pages 193-200).
